text.text:
Most founders think building an app costs $50,000.

How do I know? I have scoped 66+ products. The first question is always the same: "How much is this going to cost me?"

Here is the truth nobody tells you:

The cost is not about the app. It is about what you choose to build first.

One founder came to me with a 47-feature wishlist. Wanted all of it. Quoted $85K elsewhere.

We cut it to 1 core feature. Shipped in 3 weeks. Cost him under $8K.

That single feature got him his first 30 paying users. He added the rest later with revenue, not savings.

3 things I have learned about app costs after 66 builds:

1. If you cannot explain your app in one sentence, it is too expensive to build.

2. The right first version has 1 feature, not 15. Every extra feature doubles your risk, not your value.

3. A $3K MVP that validates beats a $50K product that nobody wanted.

The most expensive app is the one you build before you know if anyone will pay for it.

DM me "scope" and I will send you a free scope doc in 48 hours. Exact features, timeline, and cost for YOUR project. No calls. No pitch.

P.S. What is the best money saving decision you made while building your product?

text.text:
We, at Eigen Labs, have started a new podcast TheCoordinate Podcast that goes deep into the intersection of AI and crypto. AI is making intelligence digital, crypto is making institutions digital. Digital intelligence needs digital institutions. The goal of this podcast is simple: talk to the most fascinating entrepreneurs and intellectuals defining this digital future, and extract lessons from them.

For Episode 1 of TheCoordinate, I sat down with Kartik Nayak from Duke University one of the world’s leading consensus researchers, to pull consensus protocols out of the black box and build a first-principles mental model: how consensus actually works, how it evolved over 50 years, how today’s sprawling protocol families fit together, and what the next frontier of consensus research looks like.

Under the hood, there’s an intense race going on to design faster, higher-throughput, and adversary-resilient consensus protocols. Consensus directly determines retail UX and explains why Ethereum, Solana, and other L1s obsess over consensus. 

Links to the episode 1 in the thread. Hope you enjoy it.
